target.title: refactor(qa): unify live channel runtime hosting
target.body:
Closes #99699

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, and Matrix live QA commands each owned a separate runtime invocation path. Matrix also lived in its own QA runner plugin, so QA Lab could not host it through the same composable adapter registry without importing plugin-private implementation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The four existing live runtimes now contribute asynchronous adapter factories on their existing `QaRunnerCliRegistration` objects. QA Lab resolves those factories through its existing transport registry and runs their code-backed suites through the shared suite host; Matrix contributes its registration and nested factory through the owner-neutral QA runner runtime surface, so neither plugin imports the other's private modules.

The shipped registration-only QA runner contract remains a narrow compatibility mount path. It is documented by `qaRunners` plus `qaRunnerCliRegistrations` and was released through the exported `openclaw/plugin-sdk/qa-runner-runtime` subpath. Factory-backed registrations use one nested factory instead of a second public contribution array; registration-only runners continue mounting directly and cannot enter the shared suite host. Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, and Matrix all use factories.

Matrix's deterministic forced-exit behavior remains at the Matrix-owned CLI boundary. Discord is unchanged. Crabline remains on published 0.1.9 and continues using its existing in-process event observer; this change does not restore recorder polling or add a capability manifest.

## User Impact

No production channel behavior changes. QA maintainers get one adapter registry and suite-host path for the four existing live channel commands, while channel-specific credentials, scenarios, artifacts, cleanup, and plugin ownership remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto `bc802ceee189376df32049056553ff422a678293` before final validation.
- Focused proof via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` covers QA runner discovery, registration-only compatibility, registry selection, Telegram/Slack/WhatsApp adapters, shared suite lifecycle, CLI routing, Matrix factory ownership, and Matrix forced exit: 100+ tests passed across the relevant Vitest shards.
- Targeted changed production `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Codex autoreview is clean after the architecture and exact type-narrowing fixes; no accepted/actionable findings remain.
- Exact-head Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwnktj8n9yars07qvk7wb87e` passed `pnpm check:changed`, including core/core-test/extension/extension-test typechecks, core and extension lint, import-cycle checks, docs lanes, and changed-surface guards. Actions run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28693979477
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed 8/8 without changing SDK surface budgets; the factory now lives on the existing registration contribution instead of adding five named exports and a second runtime array.
